text:
luis_acme: Hey team — production pods in eu-west-1 started getting NXDOMAIN for our service endpoint api.svc.internal.acme since ~02:55 UTC. External (public) resolves fine. Impact: auth calls fail, 500s across a couple microservices. Anyone seen this pattern?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, we're on it. Can you paste a dig/nslookup output from one of the failing pods + /etc/resolv.conf? Also which VPC is this (vpc-0a1b2c3d)?

luis_acme: quick dig from pod (app-594c) in vpc-0a1b2c3d:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.svc.internal.acme A +short
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer: ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;api.svc.internal.acme.       IN  A

;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
internal.acme.     900 IN SOA ns-1.internal.acme. hostmaster.internal.acme. 2026031701 7200 900 1209600 30
```
/etc/resolv.conf shows the usual node-local cache (169.254.20.10) then VPC resolver 172.31.0.2

sam_engineer: interesting — NOERROR but no answers and an SOA for the parent zone usually means a private hosted zone exists for internal.acme with no record for that name (shadowing). Did you recently run any infra changes / terraform apply that touched Route53?

luis_acme: we did a small infra push yesterday (team infra) that added a wildcard hosted zone for "*.svc.internal.acme" to central account for service discovery. It was supposed to be for k8s SRV records only.

maya_infra: :eyes: that screams "wildcard private hosted zone shadowing the AWS-managed/private endpoint zone". For AWS interface endpoints (service-backed private DNS), if you create a private hosted zone with the same name in the VPC, it will shadow the endpoint's DNS records and return NXDOMAIN/empty responses.

alex_support: Can you confirm where that wildcard zone is associated? If it's attached to the app VPC, that would explain NXDOMAIN. We can either disassociate the hosted zone from the VPC or add the specific records, but changing records for AWS service-managed names is risky.

luis_acme: checking now — terraform state shows private hosted zone Z12345 for "svc.internal.acme" attached to vpc-0a1b2c3d and to a shared-services VPC. The zone was created by a third-party bootstrap module and has a wildcard SOA but no A/CNAME records.

sam_engineer: That matches. Wildcard private zone with no records -> SOA/no answer. Steps to repro locally: from a pod in the VPC, dig +trace api.svc.internal.acme shows query hitting the node-local cache then forwarded to the VPC resolver which returns the zone SOA.

maya_infra: dns-bot ran a quick check across accounts and found the zone is in the central account (acct-999) but associated to the customer VPC. It looks like an automated onboarding script associated the zone to the VPC during a previous migration.

alex_support: Proposed mitigation: 1) Disassociate the private hosted zone (Z12345) from the prod VPC — quick fix, will restore endpoint resolution. 2) In parallel, decide long-term: either delete the wildcard hosted zone (if not needed) or add explicit records for the service names (not recommended). 3) Add a guard in infra to prevent creating private zones that overlap AWS service namespaces.

luis_acme: We need a short downtime window? This will only change DNS resolution internally. Can you confirm it won't break other internal discovery that relies on that wildcard?

maya_infra: We verified other clusters use SRV records stored elsewhere. The wildcard was unused (no record creation). Disassociating the PHZ from vpc-0a1b2c3d should be safe. We'll schedule the change immediately if you approve.

luis_acme: please go ahead, approved. Also please note I want a rollback plan if anything odd happens.

alex_support: Proceeding: disassociating PHZ Z12345 from vpc-0a1b2c3d now. Will post results.

dns-bot: [automated] disassociate-hosted-zone Z12345 -> started by alex_support at 2026-03-17T03:45:20Z

dns-bot: [automated] disassociate-hosted-zone Z12345 -> SUCCESS (assoc removed from vpc-0a1b2c3d)

sam_engineer: quick smoke: from app pod run dig api.svc.internal.acme A +short ->
```
10.12.34.56
```
curl https://api.svc.internal.acme/health -> 200 OK

luis_acme: confirmed production traffic returning to normal, errors dropped to baseline. Huge thanks. :tada:

alex_support: Root cause summary (for ticket): wildcard private hosted zone (svc.internal.acme) created in central account and associated to customer prod VPC. It shadowed the AWS-managed/private DNS for the service endpoint and returned NOANSWER/SOA, resulting in NXDOMAIN-like failures for service lookups. Remediation: disassociate the PHZ from customer VPC. Long-term: prevent overlapping PHZ creation and add an ownership tag check in onboarding script.

luis_acme: please put the change and the guard into a postmortem and send to my team. We'll also do a quick audit for any other wildcard zones.

alex_support: will file a short postmortem and PR for infra guardrail. Closing the thread once PM is posted. :white_check_mark:
